cor.heading: Cost of Revenues
cor.text:
Cost of revenues reflects the aggregate cost incurred in the production and delivery of our products and consists of production materials, personnel costs, cost of expensed equipment and consumables, laboratory supplies, consulting costs, depreciation, production overhead costs, information technology (“IT”), maintenance and facility costs. Personnel costs consist of salaries, employee benefit costs, bonuses, and stock-based compensation expense. We expect that our cost of revenues will vary with changes in our revenues and our revenue mix.

Cost of revenues increased 3% to $185.6 million for the year ended September 30, 2025, as compared to $179.6 million for the year ended September 30, 2024. lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

s.t: In May 2025, the Company sold its DNA digital data storage business to Atlas Biosciences, Inc. ("Atlas") in exchange for 73.0 million shares of Atlas Series Seed-1 Preferred Stock, $ 2.5 million in cash, $ 2.0 million in promissory notes, contingent milestone payments of up to $ 75.0 million, and royalties on Atlas DNA data storage sales.

Simultaneously with the Agreement (see Note 6, Asset Acquisition), the Company entered into separate agreements with third-party investors to purchase shares of Series B Preferred Stock of Invenra for a consideration of $ 13.8 million to be settled by the issuance of the shares of the Company's common stock.

In February 2026, we entered into a co-exclusive license agreement with Invenra Inc. ("Invenra") for its proprietary B-Body bispecific antibody discovery platform and simultaneously acquired a 6.24% ownership interest in Invenra through the purchase of Series B Preferred Stock.
Invenra License Agreement and Investment in Equity Securities

The Company concluded that its investment in shares of preferred stock of Atlas are not in substance common stock and accounted for the investment at fair value at its acquisition date of $ 53.9 million.
On May 2, 2025, we measured the fair value of our investment in Series Seed-1 Preferred Stock of Atlas using the backsolve method with consideration for a lack of marketability.
The Company measured the fair value of our investment in Series Seed-1 Preferred Stock of Atlas using the backsolve method with consideration for a lack of marketability.

We retained an ownership stake in Atlas and may participate in the upside of DNA data storage through future technology and commercial milestone payments, and a revenue share through royalties on future sales of Atlas’ products and services.

Subsequent to the acquisition date, the Company elected to account for its investment in the preferred stock of Atlas using the measurement alternative method since Atlas is a private company, these securities do not have readily determinable fair value.
